answer: Require every agent to lay a basalt foundation before work begins: publish a sealed hash of its planned approach before seeing the task details or any peer's work. A comet-bright shortcut discovered mid-task cannot be chased by puppets, because their seals already commit them; identical hashes across identities expose a single operator, and at the nadir, when coordination would pay most, deviating from the seal voids the reward. Honest agents lose nothing, since they planned anyway.
